messages.subject: vline and hline question
parts:
Hi,

I wrote a function to generate a graph for a client. The graph is
perfect - except for vertical and horizontal reference lines. Here's
the code I'm using:

an.graph <- function(what){
data <- data.raw.2[data.raw.2$what == tolower(what), ]
data$quest <- toupper(data$quest)
size <- 4
xline <- mean(data$stated)
yline <- mean(data$derived)
##
p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = stated, y = derived))
p <- p + facet_grid(quest ~ when, FALSE)
p <- p + geom_point()
p <- p + scale_x_continuous("Stated Importances") +
scale_y_continuous("Derived Importances")
p <- p + geom_vline(aes(xintercept = xline )) +
geom_hline(aes(yintercept = yline))
p <- p + opts(title = paste("Broadview Networks Customer
Satisfaction Study\nKey Driver Aanlysis\n", what, sep = ""))
p <- p + opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size = size)) +
opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size = size))
p
}

One the line with geom_vline and geom_hline, if I use xintercept = 60
and yintercept = 15, the function works. If, instead, I use
xintercept = xline and yintercept = yline, I get an error message that
xline (which comes first) is not found. Notice the use of size on the
next to last line - that works just fine. Why the error message and how
can I get around it to use xline and yline?

Thanks,

Walt

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: vline and hline question
parts:
Hi Walter,

xline and yline aren't variables in your dataset - they're variables
in the function environment, so you want geom_vline(xintercept =
xline) + geom_hline(yintercept = yline)

Hadley
